sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition; SCSp incorporates Common Law-inspired limited partnership features)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-China BIT (signed 22 May 1981, in force 17 April 1982)
Luxembourg-United States Double Taxation Treaty (signed 20 April 2001, as amended by Protocol of 5 March 2004)
Luxembourg-Germany, Luxembourg-France, Luxembourg-Belgium and Luxembourg-Netherlands double taxation agreements (active DTAA network of over 80 treaties)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (EU freedom of establishment and free movement of capital)
EU-Singapore FTA and EU-Japan EPA (applicable to Luxembourg as an EU member state)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (laws of 13 January 2019, 25 June 2021 and subsequent amendments implementing EU AML Directives 4, 5 and 6); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 2 August 2013 (creating the SCSp); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des beneficiaires effectifs, RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the RBE; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 on anti-money laundering and terrorist financing measures; CSSF Circular 19/732; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the register of commerce and companies.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (post-CJEU restricted regime: UBO data in the RBE/LBR is not publicly accessible; authorities, the Luxembourg financial intelligence unit (cellule de renseignement financier), AML-regulated obliged entities, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest may request access; the SCSp preserves partner confidentiality because limited partner identities are not filed on the commercial register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of each general partner's and ultimate beneficial owner's passport or official national ID
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the country of origin of the partner (e.g., Chinese Notary Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin (e.g., Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs or its authorized provincial offices)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder or corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registered agent in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague-party jurisdictions, consular legalization at the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified board resolution or corporate authorization authorizing the incorporation of the Luxembourg SCSp and the appointment of the general partner or manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg registered agent and filing counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential or business address of each partner and UBO (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility company or licensed bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague-party jurisdictions; for EU banks, a simple certified copy may suffice under CSSF risk-based CDD

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter confirming the UBO or partner's source of funds for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be signed by an authorized bank officer; consular legalization is required only where the receiving Luxembourg service provider so instructs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD screening under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 19/732 against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (EU Regulation 269/2014 and EU Regulation 833/2014 and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance consolidated sanctions list); (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) FATF public statements; (iv) OFAC SDN list as prudent international benchmark; and (v) Luxembourg national locally designated persons. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) determination is mandatory under the amended Law of 12 November 2004, with the PEP definition covering domestic, EU and international PEPs. Any PEP flag or sanctions hit automatically triggers enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. Continuous automated re-screening of the SCSp general partners, limited partners, UBOs, authorized signatories and beneficial owners is required on each material transaction and at least quarterly.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) at www.lbr.lu; online pre-validation via the LBR e-Formality and MyGuichet filing interface
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filings are accepted in French, German or English; statutory corporate documents are customarily drafted in French with English courtesy translations. The corporate name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; foreign-script names must be transliterated into Latin characters. An SCSp corporate name must include or be followed by the words 'Societe en commandite speciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' in all commercial communications and RCS filings unless the name is composed solely of the personal names of the partners together with the SCSp identifier.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Assurance, Reassurance, Bourse (require prior CSSF or Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
OPCVM, SICAV, SICAR, RAIF, FCP, FIS, Fonds (require prior CSSF authorization or sectoral licensing)
Luxembourg, Grand-Duche (misleading state-affiliation implication; requires caveat or authorization)
Societe anonyme, S.A., societe a responsabilite limitee, S.a r.l. and any other corporate form label inconsistent with the actual SCSp legal form
Identical, homonymic or confusingly similar names to an existing RCS-registered legal person, trademark or trade name
Names contrary to Luxembourg public order or bonnes moeurs, or names containing criminally misleading promises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory name-reservation file; availability is determined de facto at filing by the RCS registrar. Once the proposed SCSp denomination is pre-validated through the LBR screening interface, it is conventionally held for the drafting and registration process, which in administrative practice is approximately 30 days without automatic renewal. If the RCS rejects the name, the filing counsel should: (i) within 15 days of the refusal notification, submit a corrected name re-run at the LBR with a covering letter requesting re-examination; (ii) if the registrar maintains the objection, file an administrative appeal with the Registrar citing the Law of 31 May 1999 on corporate names and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS; and (iii) if still unresolved, bring judicial proceedings before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, chambre commerciale, within one month of the final administrative refusal. In parallel, the applicant should instruct counsel to run a fresh availability check on a fallback name to avoid incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only where supplied by a licensed professional domiciliation agent approved under the amended Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies. The domiciliation agreement must provide for a physical seat in Luxembourg, correspondence handling and a legal notification service for an annual fee. A pure mail-drop arrangement without service-phase substance is not compliant. For ISIC 6201 ERP/CRM vertical cloud software activities, reviewing banks and the Luxembourg tax authorities will expect at least one Luxembourg-resident administrator or authorized manager, a paying domiciliation and administration contract, adequate local accounting records, and operational substance proportionate to the SCSp activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 5% to 10% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the CSSF, the Luxembourg financial intelligence unit (cellule de renseignement financier) or the tax inspectorate at the SCSp registered office or the registered agent's premises. The likelihood rises to approximately 20% if any UBO, PEP, sanctions-list or third-country nexus is flagged during CDD, or if the SCSp conducts significant intra-group cross-border flows without documented economic substance. As a non-licensed SaaS entity in the low-risk standard AML tier, the SCSp qualifies for simplified but not zero due diligence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR/RCS name availability pre-validation and registry clearance fee
Notarial deed or authentic instrument drafting and signature (SCSp partnership agreement executed before a Luxembourg notary, if elected; private writing alternative available)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary or formation law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market notarial scale for partnership deed and appendices

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation and legalization of foreign partner documents (passport, incumbency, power of attorney) plus apostille or consular fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator, notary of origin and competent apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per document and official statutory apostille fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg UBO register (RBE/LBR) initial declaration and filing support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE/LBR) plus filing counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR e-formality fees and nominal service fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation registration and RESA publication of the SCSp registration excerpt
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS, Recueil electronique des societes et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration and RESA publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation agent agreement, 12-month registered office and correspondence service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg domiciliation company (Ministry of Justice approved agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for domiciliation of SCSp vehicles (EUR 1,500 to 2,000 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening subscription and CDD/KYC file assembly including source-of-funds assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Screening data provider and formation counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk standard commercial entity due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal opinion and SCSp governance pack (partnership agreement, AML manual and UBO declaration templates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market legal fee for pre-incorporation due diligence and drafting package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended), Articles 102-1 to 102-13, governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) as introduced by the Loi du 12 juillet 2013 relative au partenariat; supplemented by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 November 2014 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de commerce et des sociétés - RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the authority of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Luxembourg District Court).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société (partnership agreement / articles of partnership), executed by private deed (sous seing privé) or notarial deed, filed with the RCS through the e-RCS portal together with the statutory admission declarations; the RCS and RESA publication give legal effect against third parties upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for the SCSp (EUR 0); capital amount and contribution terms are freely determined by the partners in the partnership agreement. No escrow or blocked-account certificate is required. In-kind contributions must be described and valued in the partnership agreement, and the contributing partner warrants that valuation towards third parties for five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned initial general partner and initial limited partners of [SCSp Name] (i) confirm the subscription of partnership interests set out in the partnership agreement; (ii) adopt the partnership agreement dated [date]; (iii) fix the registered office at [address], Luxembourg, and authorize the general partner to execute all Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register formalities and the RESA publication; (iv) appoint [Name] as manager, with full powers to open bank accounts, accept contributions and execute admission declarations; and (v) authorize any further registrations for value added tax, social security, and beneficial-owner transparency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of the corporate name and issuance of the negative certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS via the e-RCS online portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name-reservation application through e-RCS with three proposed names in descending preference. The RCS performs the non-confusion check against its register and issues the certificat de non-confusion, valid for one month and renewable. The name must end with SCSp or Société en commandite spéciale.
required_dossiers: Signed name-reservation request form
Copy of identity documents of the general partner
Power of attorney if filed by a third-party agent
List of three proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses the name for confusion with an existing entity, resubmit with alternative names; a refusal may be challenged before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (chambre commerciale) within 15 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The partners themselves (private deed) or a Luxembourg notary (notarial deed optional; recommended for real-property contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the contrat de société in accordance with Article 102-1 et seq. of the Companies Act. The deed must state the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, identity and contributions of the general partner (associé commandité) and limited partners (associés commanditaires), profit-sharing rules, transfer restrictions, management powers and dissolution terms. Signatures executed abroad require legalization or apostille where applicable.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Valid passport or identity document of each general and limited partner
For a corporate general partner: articles of association, recent RCS extract, list of directors and board authorization
Proof of registered office address (lease or domiciliation agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective or incomplete clauses are cured by a unanimous rectification deed (acte rectificatif) appended to and re-executed with the original partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the bank account and payment of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg or EU-licensed credit institution, supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the SCSp for the receipt of cash contributions; no minimum deposit applies. The bank issues a deposit confirmation. Contributions in kind are permitted and must be valued in the partnership agreement; a valuation report is prudent for real estate or intangible assets such as software source code.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the partnership agreement
RCS negative certificate (name reservation)
Identity and KYC documents of all partners under the Law of 12 November 2004 (AML)
Proof of registered office and corporate existence of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the credit institution requests additional KYC or source-of-funds information, provide the requested documentation within 10 business days or select an alternative Luxembourg bank; private banking decisions are not administratively appealable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation documents with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de commerce et des sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit through e-RCS the standard registration declaration form, the executed partnership agreement, the negative certificate and proof of registered office. Include the managers consent declaration. Pay the RCS filing fee of EUR 75 and the RESA publication fee of EUR 19. The RCS allocates the registration number and issues the certified extract.
required_dossiers: Standard RCS registration / admission declaration signed by the general partner
Executed partnership agreement (original or certified copy)
Negative certificate (name reservation)
Lease or domiciliation agreement for the registered office
Consent-to-act declaration of the manager(s)
Power of attorney if filing through an agent or law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a regularization query (demande de complément), file corrective documents within one month; a formal refusal may be appealed to the Tribunal d'arrondissement within 15 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RESA published by the Luxembourg RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the RCS automatically transmits the statutory particulars for publication in the RESA, which confers opposability to third parties. Verify the published extract online; no separate application or additional payment is required.
required_dossiers: Reference to the allocated RCS registration number
Registration fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published entry contains errors, submit a rectification filing to the RCS; data that is incorrectly published cannot be relied upon against third parties until corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security and beneficial-owner registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) at the RCS/LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for value added tax using form 105/A, since cloud ERP/CRM subscription revenues constitute taxable service supplies; obtain the Luxembourg VAT number. Register with the CCSS if the partnership employs or appoints salaried personnel. File the RBE declaration identifying every beneficial owner holding more than 25% of partnership interests or control rights within one month of registration.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Copy of the partnership agreement
Identification of all direct and indirect beneficial owners (25% threshold)
VAT registration application (form 105/A) and bank details
Employment notifications, if any employees will be engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late VAT registration may attract administrative fines of up to EUR 4,000; for late filings, submit a spontaneous disclosure to the AEDTV with complete KYC and track RBE declarations; outstanding CCSS contributions accrue default interest and can be regularized with penalty mitigation if self-reported.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 / NACE 62.01 pure software and cloud services. The Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) issues establishment authorizations only for regulated artisan, commercial and industrial professions; vertical ERP/CRM cloud software is an unregulated service activity requiring no such license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required. The business falls under the general freedom of establishment and is exempt from the autorisation d'établissement regime of the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to independent professions; no industrial operating license is applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Agency for the Environment)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no classed installation (établissement classé) under the Law of 10 June 1999 is present. A pure vertical-ERP/CRM cloud software office generates no industrial emissions, so no EIA report, registration or notification is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC or industrial waste discharge thresholds apply. Only general municipal waste and WEEE take-back obligations exist for office IT equipment; if the SCSp later operates its own data centers or cooling installations, F-gas reporting under Regulation (EU) 2024/573 and energy-efficiency permitting would then apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standard office occupancy clearance applies: municipal conformity certificate for the leased premises, fire-safety compliance verified by the Corps grand-ducal et de secours (CGDIS) for premises open to the public, and occupational-health duties under the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM), including compliant workstations, first-aid equipment and a documented annual risk assessment. No heavy structural-load or civil-defense clearance applies to this intellectual and cloud-based activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority; portal: impotsdirects.public.lu. VAT: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); portal: aedt.public.lu. Electronic corporate life-cycle filing via MyGuichet.lu and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR, RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate/register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and obtain the 15-digit business registration matricule number. Step 2: The ACD automatically issues the national tax identification number (TIN) for corporate-tax correspondence upon RCS activation. Step 3: File VAT registration with the AEDT to obtain a LU VAT number for taxable supplies (required for B2B cloud subscriptions and intra-EU acquisitions); non-established foreign entities may apply directly to the AEDT and must, if required, designate a Luxembourg VAT agent. Step 4: Register payroll/social accounts if the SCSp hires Luxembourg employees, and obtain a security number from the Centre commun de la securite sociale (CCSS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: the SCSp is by default fiscally transparent in Luxembourg; the partnership itself is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax; partners are taxed directly on their allocable shares of SCSp income (character and source preserved), irrespective of distribution, and non-resident partners are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income in accordance with the relevant tax treaty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Article 175bis LIR election: an SCSp carrying on a business may irrevocably elect entity-level taxation as a capital company (opting/electing partnership), subject to all-partner consent, accounting records requirements, and corporate tax rate alignment. US partners may make a check-the-box election on Form 8832 to classify a disregarded/partnership entity for US federal tax purposes; anti-hybrid rules (ATAD 2, implemented by the law of 21 December 2018) apply to neutralise mismatches where Luxembourg transparency interacts with a partner jurisdiction's entity-level taxation. No general one-stop re-classification outside these statutory channels.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Act (Loi modifiee du 12 fevrier 1979), harmonised with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic-turnover threshold: every person carrying on an independent economic activity in Luxembourg, wherever established, must apply for a Luxembourg VAT number. Domestic small-business franchise of EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (Article 159 of the VAT Act) exempts qualifying start-up businesses from charging VAT but is generally not relevant to cross-border vertical cloud B2B supplies. Euro-area intra-Community distance sales/cross-border B2C digital services use the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold and OSS/IOSS schemes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance (no API/JSON tax-stamping, no digital postmark). E-invoicing is permitted under EU Directive 2014/55/EU in PEPPOL/EN 16931 format; electronic invoices must be issued no later than the 15th day of the month following the supply. Mandatory PEPPOL e-invoicing applies to supplies to Luxembourg public-sector bodies (B2G). A transitional CTC/digital-reporting obligation for intra-EU and, on a longer deferral, domestic B2B transactions is expected under the EU VAT-in-the-Digital-Age package (2027-2030 phase-in), at which point transaction-level data, e-invoice clearance, and interoperability will replace the current periodic VAT List/EC Sales Listing framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies where goods are physically transported out of the EU by the supplier, the customer or a carrier, provided transport/exports occur within the statutory evidence window (presumptive 90 days from supply) and proof of departure is documented; intra-EU dispatches qualify for 0% only when the customer supplies a valid EU VAT identification number and the supply is reported in the EC Sales List. Services: vertical cloud/ERP/CRM B2B SaaS supplies are generally outside the Luxembourg VAT charge (Article 58 of the VAT Act - place of supply is the customer's establishment); no zero-rating claim is therefore required for non-resident business customers, but the supplier must hold buyer identification and treat the sale as reverse-charged. Services connected with exported goods (consultancy, ERP customisation for an export project) may qualify for 0% under Article 74 implementing EU Article 146(1)(e) if the foreign recipient is an entrepreneur and the services are directly linked to exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration (Single Administrative Document lodged via PLDA / Customs EDI system) with movement reference number
Commercial invoice and packing list (English-language, describing vertical-ERP cloud/hardware deliverables if any)
International transport document: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR/freight contract evidencing departure from the EU territory
Customs 'exit' confirmation from the Luxembourg Customs Administration (or transit office of exit for non-EU destinations)
Customer purchase order / SaaS agreement confirming non-resident business customer status and EU VAT ID (for intra-EU zero-rating)
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment confirmation as evidence of consideration received
Zero-rated sales ledger extract and export evidence file with audit trail linking invoice, transport and payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT law imposes an additional levy of 10% (minimum EUR 750) on any corrected VAT under-declared, rising to 100% where evasion is intentional; late VAT bears statutory interest from the due date of the relevant return. Customs law penalties (fines up to EUR 6,000, plus forfeiture remedies) apply for false export declarations. Zero-rating is retrospectively clawed back, with reversal plus the 10%/100% surcharges and interest, where the exporter cannot produce the transport/customs/payment evidence bundle or where funds are not received in the documented payment chain; criminal prosecution before Luxembourg criminal courts is possible for fraudulent export schemes (VAT carousel or sham cloud-invoicing). The VAT officer and Customs 'EVA' files remain subject to 6-10 year audit windows in fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) designated as the market conduct, AML/CFT, and payment/e-money institution supervisor for all regulated financial actors in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates under a fully liberalized capital and current account convertibility framework consistent with EU treaties. There are no exchange controls restricting inward or outward funds movement, and profit remittances from an SCSp are not subject to prior authorisation. However, cross-border transfers must carry accurate EU Balance of Payments (BoP) purpose codes and must be substantiated by the underlying partnership agreement and commercial or investment rationale to satisfy AML/CFT and tax substance reviews.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratios. Export earnings in EUR or foreign currency may be retained in local or foreign bank accounts without forced conversion, and may be freely reinvested or repatriated. Obligations are limited to statistical reporting to the BCL under the national balance of payments survey framework when transactions exceed the applicable reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg, société anonyme (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, société anonyme (BIL)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs that hold no EU/EEA passport or Luxembourg licence are not viable for opening a corporate payment account in Luxembourg. A regulated EU/EEA EMI operating through the PSD2 passporting regime into Luxembourg may serve as a supplementary rail for low-risk collections, but core treasury banking will require a domestic credit institution account. Feasibility rating: Medium conditional on the EMI having a legitimate Luxembourg presence, as the SCSp remains subject to CSSF anti-money laundering expectations and a licensed domiciliation agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors may be non-resident and physical travel is not unconditionally mandated; Luxembourg banks generally accept remote video-identification and e-signature KYC under current EU and CSSF practice for standard low-risk commercial structures. In practice, a local registered office and a certified domiciliation agent must be maintained. A live video or in-person interview is frequently reserved for enumerations involving significant cross-border capital flows, opaque intermediate holding vehicles, or where ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) in the chain present elevated risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent ownership chain with multiple foreign private investment vehicles above the SCSp
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chain-of-ownership diagram, Luxembourg Trade Register (RBE) UBO extract, certified SCSp partnership agreement, written declarations from each intermediate entity as to funding sources, and documented economic substance of the SCSp (local substance statement, client contracts, and operational records).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty base located in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and adverse-media screening outputs (EU, UN, OFSI lists), beneficial ownership certificates for each counterparty, commercial contracts substantiating genuine ERP/CRM software transactions, invoice and payment schedule, and transaction rationalisation memorandum signed by management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution disproportional to the SCSp's current annual operating expenditure or projected revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth file on contributing partners (bank statements, certified net worth summaries, asset disposal records), notarised capital contribution agreement, audited or management-prepared financial projections, capital call notice, and contemporaneous transfer instructions mirroring the statement of purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the registered office address and the actual operating location of the SCSp's cloud services business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid lease or office-sharing agreement at the registered address, utility invoice, telecom subscription records, local staffing payroll and social security declarations, and CSSF-aligned declaration that the registered office constitutes a genuine administrative location.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or loan subscriptions must be routed as SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wires from the contributing partner's bank directly to the SCSp's Luxembourg credit institution account. For reporting under EU Balance of Payments, use the appropriate BOP category for venture capital or private equity participation; practical code lies within 'S301 – Equity injection into a Luxembourg resident enterprise' for direct investment capital. The bank must receive a capital call notice and an executed fund transfer instruction describing 'capital contribution to LU_SCSP', alongside a confirmation from the SCSp's domiciliation agent, before final booking to avoid AML overflow intervention.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for ERP/CRM licensing fees, support subscriptions, and contractual vendor payments will run over SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit B2B for European counterparties, and via SWIFT MT103 and MT202 for non-EEA vendors. EUR-settled larger disbursements may be cleared via TARGET2/IBS. For significant supplier agreements, an irrevocable documentary credit (Commercial LC) opened at a Luxembourg credit institution is permissible. All outbound transfers must state a valid purpose code, reference the underlying contract, and conform to the bank's economic substance checklist.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with OTC execution through a regulated EU bank or licensed broker
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for convertibility of ERP/CRM cloud subscription cash flows
Vanilla EUR/USD FX swaps and options (including collars and participating forward structures) transacted under EMIR clearing thresholds for non-financial counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation statement (déclaration de mise à jour) to the Luxembourg RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following each anniversary of the initial RCS registration; filed electronically through the e-RCS portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SCSp's manager to a €500.00 administrative fine; repeated omissions for more than six months can trigger an adverse RCS notice and, after judicial notification, administrative strike-off (radiation).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (annual financial statements) and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end (for a 31 December year-end, by 30 September of the following year); the filing must be published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default triggers a €125.00 penalty for filings up to one month late and €250.00 beyond that period; sustained non-compliance gives rise to a RCS court petition for compulsory dissolution and strike-off of the partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (no-change declaration) in the UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 March, even if no ownership change occurred; updates for any shareholding transfer must be filed within 15 days of the operation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from €300.00 to €10,000.00 per infraction; knowingly false declarations carry criminal penalties of imprisonment and additional fines, and may affect the partner's entitlement to contractual advantages.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Luxembourg law requires SCSp companies to appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) when any two of the following three criteria are exceeded at the balance sheet date: total assets EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50 employees. An audit becomes unconditionally mandatory for regulated undertakings, public-interest entities, or when partners holding at least 10% of the capital or voting rights so request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in compliance with the Law of 19 June 2009 on annual accounts, transposing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts and facilities for cross-border groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must keep a written register of beneficial owners at its registered office. Any transfer of a partnership interest obliges the manager to send a UBO update within 15 days of the transfer. In addition, a no-change annual confirmation is due by 31 March each year; the managing partner must first obtain and retain evidence of each ultimate beneficial owner's identity and percentage of interest before the transfer can be recorded. Failure to complete the UBO protocol makes the transfer ineffective towards third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$4,000 – US$9,000 per annum for a licensed Luxembourg registered office and domiciliation agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$12,000 – US$35,000 per annum for a certified audit in the relevant size segment

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17.00% CIT on taxable income above EUR 175,000; 15.00% below EUR 175,000; plus 7.00% solidarity surcharge (maximum combined 18.19%); municipal business tax variable, e.g. 6.75% in Luxembourg City. A SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not subject to entity-level CIT when treated as pass-through.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp carries no entity-level effective CIT rate (0.00% at entity level). Partners benefit from Luxembourg IP box (80% exemption on net qualifying IP income), participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, notional interest deduction, and treaty relief on redistribution. Non-resident partners are generally taxable only in their country of residence unless a Luxembourg taxable permanent establishment exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (corporate income tax return for collective entities); SCSp files via the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration online portal (eCDF / MyGuichet) as an informative pass-through return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed by 31 May following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension to 31 December for returns prepared by an approved Luxembourg tax adviser; further extension is discretionary on application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, RCS number, registered office, fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be identified with full legal name, registered address, and state of tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before tax allocation: revenue, operating expenses, net income, depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source items attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment; exclude offshore cloud and licence income unless effectively connected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit allocation schedule among general and limited partners according to the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert each non-resident partner's profit share and capital account adjustments; state treaty-based allocation rights.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of related-party transactions and transfer pricing method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intra-group software licensing and CRM cloud fees with benchmarked arm's length prices; indicate if a local file / master file is attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax summary: dividends, interest, and royalties paid during the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show residency certificate reference for each non-resident payee and confirm treaty rate claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss compensation statement and carryforward utilisation calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may only utilise losses to the extent attributab le to a Luxembourg permanent establishment and not otherwise used in the home jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties up to EUR 2,500; late payment interest at 3% per annum; an administrative fine of 10% to 25% of the tax assessed for wilful non-compliance; criminal prosecution for intentional false statements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15.00% domestic dividend withholding tax for opaque Luxembourg companies; 0.00% for qualifying distributions under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or Luxembourg participation exemption. SCSp distributions are generally not subject to entity-level WHT because the partnership is fiscally transparent; tax may arise at partner level, and underlying Luxembourg company distributions retain source character.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the partner must submit a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership and ownership-duration declaration, and the Luxembourg withholding tax relief / refund application (Form 250/251 series) before payment or within three years for refund. Certification of residency is mandatory; failure to file pre-payment triggers full 15% statutory withholding tax with later refund only if treaty evidence is supplied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg WHT is 0.00% on outbound royalties and 0.00% on most outbound interest payments. Treaty rates typically confirm 0% for royalties and 0%-15% for interest depending on the partner jurisdiction; profit-sharing loans and certain hybrid debt instruments may attract higher source-state treatment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 aggregate related-party revenue threshold for mandatory Local File; Master File required where group consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000; Country-by-Country Report threshold matches the OECD at EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg recognises OECD-aligned arm's length and anti-hybrid rules. It has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations for non-EU zero-tax jurisdictions, but ATAD, DAC-6, the General Anti-Abuse Rule, and Luxembourg's substance circulars require real economic activity for SCSp entities to access treaty benefits and prevent constructive shell classification. Genuine business decisions, employees, office premises, accounting records, and bank accounts in Luxembourg are essential.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Luxembourg-source profits in the SCSp return, false partner allocation, suppression of ERP/CRM subscription income, or presenting a fictitious non-resident beneficial owner to avoid taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of one to five years; additional administrative surcharge of 10%-25%; default interest at 3% per annum; confiscation of proceeds and complete reassessment of five prior fiscal years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing partners who sign false returns may have the corporate veil pierced; personal civil liability for evaded tax, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a SCSp with no real business, no employees, no Luxembourg decision-making, no office, and using it solely to strip income through artificial cloud licences or to access an aggressive double tax treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of the SCSp as opaque, addition of withholding tax on deemed distributions, CFC income inclusion in shareholders' tax base, penalty of 100% of tax understated, and mandatory substance documentation failure penalties under ATAD/GAAR.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered personally to pay the tax differential, restitution of treaty benefits with interest, management ban up to ten years, and criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and verify ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp, non-submission to the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners, or obscuring the ownership of the ERP/CRM vertical cloud entity in a manner that facilitates money laundering via invoicing or Stripe Billing / Direct Debit payment flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for legal entities; regulatory sanctions against the RBE processing entity; imprisonment of senior officers up to five years for deliberate money laundering facilitation; publication of penal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and senior managers face personal non-capped civil liability for laundering damages, travel bans pending criminal investigation, freezing of bank accounts, and disqualification from directorship for ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length intra-group royalties for software IP, CRM platform access, or technical support to escape Luxembourg taxation; absence of contemporaneous TP documentation for related-party transactions; migration of IP to a zero-tax jurisdiction without adequate buy-out price.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment at arm's length with upward profit adjustment, additional tax up to 25%-50% of understatement, interest, late filing penalty up to EUR 2,500, exclusion of loss compensation, and reclassification of royalty payments as constructive dividends subject to 15% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax officers may be jointly and severally liable for the re-assessed tax and penalties if they knowingly failed to prepare TP documentation; may be subject to civil restitution, travel restriction orders, and criminal sentences for tax evasion up to five years.
